findings.claim: beans-and-bean-scopes is listed in lab.json covers (line 9), and module.json sourceCoverageNotes line 27 says the lab has 'at least one tested task for each of the nine taught topics', but no task gives the learner executable work on that topic. The author's only mapping is the covers entry plus the beans topic.json pointer to the module lab ('lab': 'module:spring-boot-basics'). lab.json objectives (lines 16-26) name no beans-and-bean-scopes objective, the lab-run.json testScope maps no task to it, and the partial-coverage note (module.json line 29) does not mention it. The learner does meet a bean: Task 1 (README line 60) and the WorkshopCatalog Javadoc say that CatalogConfig turns the catalog into a bean, which Task 1 injects. That is reading about a finished registration, not doing one. The topic's objectives are o1 (register a bean by stereotype plus scanning and by a @Bean method in a @Configuration class, and choose between them), o2 (predict singleton versus prototype sharing) and o3 (a stateless singleton keeps no per-request fields). The page practices o1 in Activity 2, 'Two ways to register a bean', where the learner writes a @Configuration class with a @Bean method and annotates their own class. In the lab, CatalogConfig ships complete and is marked 'you do not edit it' (CatalogConfig.java line 9). AboutController ships already annotated. Task 1 only consumes the existing bean through constructor injection, which is dependency-injection-replacing-manual-wiring#o1, and Task 7 only widens scanning. A learner can pass all nine tests without registering a bean, choosing a registration route or reasoning about scope. Under the captain rule that a module lab covers every taught topic with executable learner work, and with no compensation allowed, this topic is uncovered while the catalog says it is covered.
findings.recommendation: Make bean registration learner work inside the existing Task 1 rather than adding a task. Ship CatalogConfig with its seed-building method body intact but without the configuration-class and bean-method annotations, and add CatalogConfig.java (Task 1) to the What-you-edit table. Change its do-not-edit comment to a TODO that asks the learner to register the seeded catalog by the route the beans page recommends for a class whose construction needs logic. Update the WorkshopCatalog Javadoc to match. The existing task1 test then fails until both the registration and the injection are done; if the learner injects first, the missing-bean startup failure taught on the dependency-injection page appears. Add beans-and-bean-scopes#o1 to lab.json objectives. In the module.json partial-coverage note, record that o2 and o3 (scopes) stay on the page. Re-run the solved and starter runs, because starter bytes change. Time: this adds about 3 minutes (two annotations on a shipped method). Either raise lab.json tasks to 39, which uses up the 1-minute S2 slack and so needs the S2 arithmetic in module.json line 28 reworked (for example by moving the page overflow), or save the time inside Task 7, as spring-basics-lab9-edu-002 allows. Do not leave the 36 unchanged without saying so.

findings.claim: Three of the four new tasks can be passed by transcription, so their tests show that the learner copied a line, not that they used the topic's idea. Task 6 (README line 89, What-you-edit line 22) gives the full file path and both setting lines verbatim. The idea it should exercise, where a generated project keeps its settings (generating page, Activity 2 row 'The server.port setting' and the cheat sheet), is stated for the learner. Task 7 (line 97) gives the exact annotation attribute and its complete value list. The taught idea it should exercise is that scanning starts at the main class package and that naming base packages replaces that default (auto-configuration page, Activity 2 and 'The composite, written out'). Task 9 (line 111) gives the exact startup call. The idea it should exercise, an embedded server started from your own main (spring-vs-spring-boot page, Activity 1 and Activity 2 row 'An embedded Tomcat started from your main method'), is supplied instead of recalled. The TODO comments in WorkshopsApplication.java (lines 9-11 and 16-18) repeat the same answers. The pages ground all three tasks well, and Task 8 is a genuine fresh problem: the learner must read the shipped OpenAPI document as the openapi page's Activity 2 teaches. Tasks 6, 7 and 9 are not faded at all, though the S2 block they sit in is the calendar's 'Faded, then fresh problem' block. The README's Test section correctly says the tests do not check how the code is written, so this does not mislead. It does weaken the evidence behind three of the nine coverage claims.
findings.recommendation: Fade the three tasks in README and in the TODO comments, without changing tests. Task 6: give the two setting keys and values, but ask the learner to create the file where a generated project keeps its settings, pointing to the generating page's Activity 2. Change the What-you-edit row to 'application.properties (you create it; where is part of Task 6)' and keep the src/main/java warning as a Troubleshooting entry. Task 7: state the symptom and the rule ('a package list replaces the default'), and let the learner choose either the three-annotation form they practiced in the auto-configuration page's Activity 2 or the shortcut attribute. The README may name that attribute, because the page does not, but not its value list. Task 9: replace the literal call with 'start Spring Boot from main the way a generated project's main class does', pointing to the spring-vs-spring-boot page's Activity 1. Time: recall instead of copying adds a little time to Tasks 6, 7 and 9 (about 1 minute each for a learner who did the pages). State in lab.json minutes and the module.json line 28 arithmetic whether the 36 still holds or the S2 split changes. If there is no room, fade only Task 7 and Task 9 and leave Task 6 as it is.

findings.claim: The new S2 arithmetic (module.json line 28) gets its 1 minute of slack by silently dropping the practice mastery check. The previous version of this note budgeted 'the check takes up to 15' inside the same 40-minute block. module.json still declares that check in its assessments array (line 21) and in sourceCoverageNotes line 30 as 'learner-visible practice.gift, ungraded, 15 minutes at most'. Its bound blueprint still has dayId S2 and instructions that place it 'before the module coding lab' (fact cited only for scheduling; content not reviewed). Either the check is still a learner-facing S2 item, and Standard S2 then needs 58 page + 15 check + 36 lab = 109 minutes in the 95 minutes the four page blocks and the coding-lab block give (14 over), or it is retired under the captain rule that no module-mastery practice layer exists, and module.json does not say so. Either way the 'S2 stays within 120 minutes' sentence does not account for a learner-visible item that the catalog still lists for S2. The partial-coverage note itself (line 29) is now free of mastery-check compensation, which is correct.
findings.recommendation: In module.json only: rewrite sourceCoverageNotes line 30 to say that the legacy practice mastery check is not scheduled on S2 and is not part of the module's practice or coverage (retirement or relocation to be decided on a separate branch). Or, if it stays learner-facing on S2, add its up-to-15 minutes back into the line 28 arithmetic and cut the lab's task minutes or move the check off S2 to match. Do not leave the 15 minutes unaccounted for.

findings.claim: README line 15 now gives the task estimate (36 minutes, 'after the one-time setup'), but nothing tells the learner when to run the 8-minute online setup or which day and block the lab runs in. The only place the lab fits on Standard is S2's 40-minute block, with 37 minutes left after the pages (module.json line 28), and only if setup has already been done outside the block. A learner who opens the bundle at the start of that block and follows the README top to bottom spends 8 + 36 = 44 minutes, which overruns the block. The sibling required Spring labs name their day in README line 5 (validation-errors-and-testing: 'the required lab of the Standard track's error-handling day'; api-security: '... security day'). The html-css-js/dom-tooling-and-async README line 3 names its day and block and tells the learner to do the one-time setup before the block.
findings.recommendation: Extend the Goal sentence on line 14 or 15: the lab runs on Standard S2 in the 40-minute coding block after the four S2 pages, and the learner should run the Setup command once while online before that block. This is a README byte change, so batch it with any edit from spring-basics-lab9-edu-002 and the mirrored learner-repo sync.

findings.claim: lab.json line 23 now claims path-query-and-body-parameters#o2 ('Predict the response status when a required query parameter is missing or a path variable cannot be converted to the declared type'). Task 8's test checks only the missing-parameter half, and the 400 is stated in the shipped OpenAPI document rather than predicted by the learner. No test sends a non-numeric path variable or groupSize, although the page's Activity 1 and its Recap teach the conversion case and the fixture's 400 description names it. The module.json partial-coverage note (line 29) says Task 8 adds 'the required query parameter and its 400 that path-query-and-body-parameters#o1 and #o2 name'. That sentence reads as full coverage of #o2 and does not record the untested conversion half, unlike the other partial claims it lists.
findings.recommendation: Add one clause to the module.json partial-coverage note: for path-query-and-body-parameters#o2, Task 8 checks the 400 for a missing required query parameter but not a failed conversion, which stays on the page (Activity 1). Alternatively, add one MockMvc request to the existing task8 test with a non-numeric groupSize that expects 400, at no extra learner work for a correct int binding.
